title: rpc : add bounds check in rdma_recv
body:
## Overview

In `socket_t::impl::rdma_recv()` (`ggml/src/ggml-rpc/transport.cpp`), incoming completions are copied into `data` without checking if `wc.byte_len` fits within `rem`.

When `rpc_serve_client()` reads the initial command byte into a 1-byte stack variable (`sock->recv_data(&cmd, 1)`), an incoming completion with `wc.byte_len > 1` causes `memcpy` to overflow the stack buffer and underflow `rem -= got`.

This adds a check (`got > rem`) before the copy, logs the error with `LOG_ERROR`, reposts the receive slot so the ring isn't depleted, and returns false to close the connection.

## Additional information

Tested locally with ASan on SoftRoCE (`rxe0`). Sending > 1 byte for `cmd` triggers `stack-buffer-overflow` in `memcpy` without this check. With this check, the overrun is caught early and the connection drops cleanly without memory corruption.
